question: Which of following tribes celebrates the Rongker festival?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karbi**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Karbi Rongker festival is a major annual festival celebrated by the **Karbi tribe of Assam** to seek blessings for a prosperous harvest and the well-being of the community.
 
• It is usually observed in **January-February**, marking the beginning of the new year for the Karbi people.
 
• The festival involves various rituals, including sacrifices of animals like **chickens and pigs,** as offerings to the deities to ensure good health, protection from natural calamities, and peace.
 
• Several deities, including Hemphu, Mukar, and Bark Arnam, are worshiped during the festival, each representing different aspects of life such as **agriculture, health, and nature.**
 
• It is a community-centric festival with cultural performances, dances, and songs, where the entire tribe comes together to celebrate, reinforcing social bonds and traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hornbill Festival (Nagaland)**

 
 
• Often referred to as the "**Festival of Festivals,**" the Hornbill Festival showcases the rich cultural heritage of the **Naga tribes.**
 
• It includes traditional music, dance, art, and food, celebrated **annually in December.**
 
• The festival aims to promote **inter-tribal interaction** and preserve Naga culture.
 
 
 
• **Bihu Festival (Assam)**
 
 
• Celebrated primarily by the Assamese people, **Bihu marks the agricultural cycle** and has three main forms **Bohag Bihu (spring festival), Kati Bihu (autumn festival), and Magh Bihu (winter festival).**
 
• It involves traditional dances, songs, and feasting.
 
 
 
• **Pongal (Tamil Nadu)**
 
 
• Celebrated by the **Tamil community**, Pongal is a harvest festival that lasts for four days.
 
• It includes cooking the traditional dish "Pongal" and various rituals to honor the Sun God, cattle, and the Earth.
 
 
 
• **Makar Sankranti (Various States)**
 
 
• While celebrated **across India**, many tribal communities have their unique ways of observing Makar Sankranti.
 
• It signifies the transition of the Sun into Capricorn and includes kite flying, bonfires, and community feasting.
 
 
 
• **Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra)**
 
 
• This festival marks the Maharashtrian New Year and the arrival of spring.
 
• It involves erecting the **"Gudi" (a symbolic flag),** traditional sweets, and various cultural activities like folk dances.
